evidence: app/src/routes/(home).ts:1-2 — core defineRoute + server-html html, the documented API of the current stable 0.11.0 (verified against @gracile/engine@0.12.0 dist/routes/route.d.ts)
app/server.js:3,16 — @gracile/gracile/hono honoAdapter + getClientBuildPath, public exports of 0.11.0 (dist/hono.d.ts) and the official Hono starter pattern
app/src/lib/build.ts:8 — url.hostname === 'gracile-static' relies on an @internal build behavior (packages/engine/src/routes/render.ts), the only non-documented reliance
app/package.json:11-15 — all five deps pinned to current stable latest (gracile 0.11.0, vite 8.3.5, hono 4.13, @hono/node-server 2.1.5); no -next/beta/canary tags
app/src/routes/(home).client.ts:7 — vanilla custom elements instead of Lit hydration/islands, avoiding Gracile's newer progressive-hydration surface
reach.rationale: No experimental/preview APIs at all, but the entire app rests on the documented surface of a self-described alpha, pre-1.0 framework whose current release is only ~6 months old, plus one reliance on an undocumented @internal build behavior.

evidence: app/src/lib/build.ts:1-8 — the single fragile reliance is wrapped in one 9-line module with a written rationale; routes consume it via one import
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:284 — routes call isBuildRender(url) rather than inlining the hostname sniff
app/src/routes/(home).client.ts:7-80 and app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.ts:7-77 — client enhancements are self-contained vanilla custom elements with no framework hydration plumbing to swap
containment.rationale: The only thing that could change underneath the app (the build-render stub origin) is isolated behind a single trivially swappable wrapper; everything else is documented core framework usage.

evidence: app/src/lib/build.ts:1-8 — the guard is required by SPEC.md's hard 'no API data at build time' rule, given Gracile renders every route during vite build (@gracile/engine plugin-client-build.ts); no documented signal exists in the stub handler context
app/vite.config.ts:5 — output: 'server' is the minimal, documented config; no experimental flags such as pages.premises.expose
app/server.js:1-20 — Hono adapter usage is the framework's documented production-server path (official minimal-server-hono starter)
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.ts:38-76 — DOMParser-based partial swap keeps interactivity dependency-free where Lit hydration would add framework-coupling risk
justification.rationale: Every framework API used is either mandatory (routing, document, server adapter) or the most conservative available option; the one undocumented sniff has no stable alternative and serves a spec requirement.

findings.issue: isBuildRender detects the build-time render by matching the undocumented 'gracile-static' stub hostname used inside @gracile/engine's @internal render pipeline; a rename or behavior change in any future release would silently make the production build fetch API data (or crash), violating the spec constraint
findings.suggestion: Keep the guard but make it fail loudly: centralize (already done), add a comment pinning the version it was verified against, and add a secondary safety (e.g., an env flag passed during build, or a graceful fallback if the hostname sniff ever stops matching); ideally upstream a documented build-render flag in the handler context to Gracile

findings.issue: @gracile/gracile ^0.11.0 is a caret range on a pre-1.0, self-described alpha framework whose minor releases can carry breaking changes (gracile.js.org/docs: 'This project is in an alpha state')
findings.suggestion: Pin the exact version and rely on the lockfile; re-verify route/server APIs against release notes on every upgrade since 0.x minors may break

findings.issue: Stylesheet href is built via new URL('./document.css', import.meta.url).pathname rather than the documented root-relative pattern (Gracile docs show <link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/styles/...">), so the URL form depends on undocumented Vite/Gracile resolution details
findings.suggestion: Use the documented root-relative path literal, which the framework resolves explicitly

summary: The app is refreshingly conservative: it uses only the documented core APIs of the mandated Gracile 0.11 release, pins every dependency to a current stable version with no beta/canary tags, and deliberately skips the whole @gracile-labs experimental ecosystem in favor of vanilla custom elements and standard platform APIs. The single risky spot is an isolated hostname sniff that detects the framework's undocumented @internal build-time render to honor the spec's no-build-time-fetching rule — justified, contained, but worth a pin-and-comment or an upstream request for a documented signal.
